## 1. Goal

Write, in Ahaana's own words, a caption and a one-paragraph "what this graph shows" for every figure, for the results chapter and her part of the viva.

## 2. Background

**From BLUEPRINT §6:**

| # | Question | What we vary | Graph |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| E1 | Which scheduler gives the lowest average wait? | Load: light, medium, heavy (arrival rate) | Average wait vs load, one line per scheduler |
| E2 | Which scheduler prevents starvation? | Same runs as E1 | Maximum wait vs load; plus a wait distribution (CDF), as in Fan & Liang Fig. 5 |
| E3 | Are priorities respected? | Priority mix | Average wait per priority level, with and without aging. Inspired by Becker & Schüle, who report per-application flow time with and without aging in tables; we plot wait per priority level |
| E4 | How does the aging rate α change the trade-off? | α from 0 to 1 (alpha_milli 0 to 1,000) | Average wait of high-priority jobs vs maximum wait of low-priority jobs |
| E5 | When does reservation pay off? | Share of big-memory jobs (0% to 40%) | Maximum wait with and without reservation |
| E6 | How close is each scheduler to optimal? | Tiny cases, 6 to 9 jobs, 200 instances (50 per job count) | Ratio of each scheduler's **total turnaround** to the exact optimum's total turnaround (box plot), plus the absolute wait gap (scheduler total wait − optimal total wait). Turnaround = wait + duration, so the optimal schedule is the same as for total wait and the ratio is never undefined; no instance is skipped. The caption says that, unlike the Beaumont survey, which divides by a lower bound (the area bound), we divide by the exact optimum; whiskers follow the same convention (1.5 × the interquartile range) |

**From PRD §10A Demo row 7:**

| # | Time | Who | On screen | Says | If it breaks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | 8:30–10:30 | Ahaana | Graphs E1, E2, E5, E6 | What each graph shows and how to read it; each point is a mean over 30 seeds with a 95% confidence interval; the E6 box plot compares each scheduler with the exact optimum | Graphs are also in the report PDF |

**From PRD §10A Likely questions (Ahaana):**

| Question | Answer owner |
| --- | --- |
| What do the error bars mean? | Ahaana: each point is the mean over 30 seeds; the bar is the 95% confidence interval of that mean, from the Student-t distribution |
| Why a box plot for E6, and why turnaround? | Ahaana: it shows the spread over all instances, not just the average; turnaround keeps the ratio defined when the optimum has zero wait |

## 3. Scope

**In scope:**

- A caption per figure (what is plotted, units, n seeds, what the bars mean)
- One paragraph per figure: what it shows and how to read it
- E6 caption: we divide by the exact optimum, not a lower bound as in Beaumont; whiskers 1.5 × IQR

**Out of scope:**

- Method and statistics text (K-40)

## 9. How to verify

Rehearsal recording or notes in the PR.

## 10. Viva notes

**Idea:** a figure is only evidence if the audience knows how to read it.
**Examiner question:** "What do the error bars mean?" — Each point is the mean over 30 seeds; the bar is the 95% confidence interval of that mean, from the Student-t distribution.

## 11. Pitfalls

- Describing sample (fake) figures
- Claiming more than the confidence intervals support
